evals.prompt: Our order service calls the pricing service on the hot path, and it is a JSON REST call today. Should we move it to gRPC?
evals.expected_output: Selects the internal paradigm by constraint (latency, streaming, schema-first) rather than preference, notes the proxy and browser cost of gRPC, and warns about chaining synchronous internal hops.

value: Internal service-to-service, low latency, streaming, schema-first
assertions.description: Matches the paradigm to the internal hot-path constraint

value: Never chain more than 2 synchronous internal hops

evals.prompt: We need to push live order status to the customer's browser. The team wants WebSockets.
evals.expected_output: Chooses SSE for a server-push-only flow, reserves WebSocket for bidirectional needs, and names the reconnect and load-balancer affinity costs.

assertions.description: Picks the one-directional option for a one-directional need
Names the cost of the connection-based option

evals.prompt: A partner wants us to notify them whenever an order ships. What do we build?
evals.expected_output: Specifies an outbound webhook with signature verification, a bounded retry policy with backoff, and an idempotency key, and refuses to treat any of the three as optional.

value: No webhook without signature, retry policy, and idempotency key
